class.name: WebSVG
class.brief_description: A control that renders a scriptable SVG document inside a CSS-faithful box.
class.description: [WebSVG] mimics the HTML [code]<svg>[/code] element. The node's rect [member Control.size] is the SVG [code]width[/code]/[code]height[/code]: the SVG content is drawn at 1:1 scale and, when the node is resized, it is clipped rather than scaled — exactly like an [code]<svg>[/code] with no [code]viewBox[/code]. The element is wrapped by the CSS box model: [code]border[/code], [code]background[/code], [code]box-shadow[/code], [code]border-radius[/code] and padding come from the [theme_item style] theme item (a [StyleBoxCSS]), while [theme_item box_sizing] controls whether the node size is the content box or border box. With the default [code]content-box[/code] sizing, border and padding grow outward from the node size; with [code]border-box[/code] they are drawn inside it and the content area shrinks. A document can come from three places, and all three run the same pipeline (decode, sanitize, inline external resources, parse): - [member svg_markup] — markup typed or pasted directly, as in an HTML [code]<svg>[/code] element. - [member svg_source] — a [code].svg[/code] file dragged in from the FileSystem dock. [code].svg[/code] files import as [DPITexture], which carries the source markup, so no separate import step is needed. - [member svg_file_path] — a path, which may point outside the project or at [code]user://[/code]. [method load_svg_file] and [method load_svg_bytes] do the same thing at runtime, which is how an application lets its own users pick and swap artwork. Markup is rendered verbatim, so [code]<defs>[/code], gradients, [code]<clipPath>[/code] and filters survive. Elements the typed DOM does not model are preserved as [WebSVGRaw] child nodes, so editing one shape never discards the rest of an imported document. Imported documents are treated as untrusted input. [member sanitize] strips [code]<script>[/code], [code]on*[/code] event handlers, unsafe [code]href[/code] schemes and [code]<!DOCTYPE>[/code] internal subsets; [member inline_external_resources] rewrites referenced images to [code]data:[/code] URIs so the document is self-contained and renders identically here and in a browser. Default values reproduce the browser user-agent stylesheet for [code]<svg>[/code]: a transparent background, no border, no shadow, no padding and content-box sizing.

method.name: get_border_box
method.description: Returns the border box in local coordinates. Equals [code]Rect2(Vector2(), size)[/code] under [code]border-box[/code] sizing; under [code]content-box[/code] it grows beyond the node size by the border and padding.

method.name: parse_svg
method.description: Parses a full SVG markup string (including inline [code]style[/code] and any [code]<defs>[/code]/gradients), sets the node size from [method get_intrinsic_size], applies box CSS from the root [code]<svg style="…">[/code], rebuilds the scriptable child DOM, and renders the markup verbatim. The markup passes through the same sanitizing and resource-inlining steps as a loaded file, governed by [member sanitize] and [member inline_external_resources].

method.name: to_svg_string
method.description: Serializes the current document back to an SVG markup string.

method.name: get_computed_style
method.description: Returns a dictionary describing the fully resolved box geometry and paint values: the [code]border_box[/code], [code]padding_box[/code] and [code]content_box[/code] rectangles, the resolved per-side [code]border_width[/code], [code]border_color[/code] and [code]border_style[/code] arrays (ordered left, top, right, bottom), [code]padding[/code], [code]corner_radius[/code] (ordered top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left), [code]background_color[/code], [code]background_clip[/code], [code]box_sizing[/code] and the list of [code]box_shadows[/code]. This is the canonical "what the engine actually computed" snapshot used by the headless testing bridge to compare against a real browser's [code]getComputedStyle()[/code].

method.name: get_content_box
method.description: Returns the content box: the border box inset by the border widths and then by the padding. This is where the SVG content is drawn.

method.name: get_padding_box
method.description: Returns the padding box: the border box inset by the border widths.

method.name: load_svg_file
method.description: Loads and renders the SVG document at [param path], which may be a [code]res://[/code] resource, a [code]user://[/code] file, or an absolute path outside the project. Handles gzip-compressed [code].svgz[/code] files, a byte order mark, and UTF-8 or UTF-16 encoding. [code]res://[/code] paths are resolved through [ResourceLoader] first, so they keep working in an exported project where the original [code].svg[/code] is replaced by its imported [DPITexture]. Relative [code]<image href>[/code] references are resolved against the file's own directory.

method.name: load_svg_bytes
method.description: Loads a document already held in memory — downloaded, generated, or read by the application itself. Accepts the same encodings and compression as [method load_svg_file]. [param base_dir] is the directory relative [code]<image href>[/code] references resolve against; leave it empty when the document has no external references.

method.name: reload_source
method.description: Re-reads [member svg_source] or [member svg_file_path], bypassing the resource cache, so edits made to the file on disk are picked up. Returns [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] when neither is set.

method.name: clear
method.description: Discards the document along with [member svg_source] and [member svg_file_path], leaving the node empty.

method.name: get_intrinsic_size
method.description: Returns the document's own size, following the CSS rules for replaced elements: the root [code]width[/code] and [code]height[/code] when both are absolute lengths, otherwise the [code]viewBox[/code] size, otherwise the [code]300 x 150[/code] default. Loading a document sets [member Control.size] to this, so artwork renders at its natural size unless [member fit] says otherwise.

method.name: get_view_box
method.description: Returns the document's [code]viewBox[/code]. Meaningful only when [method has_view_box] returns [code]true[/code].

method.name: has_view_box
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the document declares a usable [code]viewBox[/code].

method.name: get_document_info
method.description: Returns what parsing found: [code]intrinsic_size[/code], [code]has_intrinsic_size[/code], [code]view_box[/code], [code]has_view_box[/code], [code]preserve_aspect_ratio[/code], [code]element_count[/code], [code]has_animations[/code], [code]source_mode[/code], [code]dom_built[/code], plus three string arrays: [code]unsupported[/code] (features that will not render), [code]removed[/code] (active content sanitizing stripped) and [code]warnings[/code] (external references that could not be resolved).

method.name: get_unsupported_features
method.description: Returns the features the document uses that the renderer cannot draw, such as [code]<pattern>[/code] or filter primitives other than [code]feGaussianBlur[/code]. Empty when the document renders completely.

method.name: get_document_status
method.description: Returns a human-readable summary of [method get_document_info], shown read-only in the Inspector.

members.member: Entry point for pasting SVG markup. Setting it calls [method parse_svg]; reading it returns [method to_svg_string]. Setting this by hand clears [member svg_source] and [member svg_file_path], because the two input methods are alternatives — otherwise the next reload would silently overwrite the edit. While a file source is set this property is hidden from the Inspector and not stored in the scene: the file is the source of truth, and handing a real-world SVG (tens of kilobytes, often on a single line) to a multiline text field costs seconds every time the property list rebuilds. [member document_status] carries the summary, and scripts can still read the markup here or through [method to_svg_string].

An [code].svg[/code] file to render, normally set by dragging one in from the FileSystem dock. Setting this clears [member svg_file_path]. Relative [code]<image href>[/code] references resolve against the resource's directory. How the markup is obtained depends on how the file was imported: - Imported as [DPITexture], the resource itself carries the SVG source, so the document travels with the scene and works in an exported project. - Imported as a raster texture — the default for [code].svg[/code], since [code]ResourceImporterTexture[/code] claims the extension first — the resource holds only pixels, so the markup is read from the file on disk instead. That works in the editor, but the original [code].svg[/code] is not packed into an export. The node raises a scene-tree warning saying so; resolve it by setting [b]Import As[/b] to [b]DPITexture[/b] and reimporting, by enabling [member embed_source], or by using [member svg_file_path]. Assigning a texture that is not an SVG at all leaves nothing to render, and is reported the same way.

Path of an [code].svg[/code] or [code].svgz[/code] file to render. Unlike [member svg_source] this may point at [code]user://[/code] or outside the project, which is what makes it usable for files an application's own user chooses. Accepts drag and drop from the FileSystem dock. Setting this clears [member svg_source].

Read-only summary of the loaded document: its size, element count, and any unsupported features, removed content or unresolved references. See [method get_document_info] for the same information in a form scripts can use.
The stored copy of the document kept when [member embed_source] is enabled. Written by the node; there is no reason to set it directly.

When [code]true[/code], a copy of the loaded document is stored in the scene alongside the file reference, and is used if the file cannot be read later. Off by default: the copy makes the scene self-contained but duplicates the whole document into it, once per node.

Whether the document is mirrored into scriptable child [WebSVGElement] nodes. Building the DOM is what makes individual shapes addressable from code, but it costs a [Node] per element, which is a poor trade for a large imported file nobody intends to edit. [constant DOM_AUTO] builds the DOM for markup, and for a file only when it contains SMIL animation — which [WebSVGAnimation] can only play back from the typed DOM.

Whether to strip active content from the document while loading: [code]<script>[/code] and [code]<foreignObject>[/code] elements, [code]on*[/code] event handlers, [code]href[/code] values with a scheme such as [code]javascript:[/code] or a remote URL, and [code]<!DOCTYPE>[/code] internal subsets, which is how entity-expansion attacks arrive. Leave this on for any document the application did not author itself, especially when the markup will be served as part of a web page. What was removed is reported by [method get_document_info].

Whether [code]<image>[/code] elements referencing local files are rewritten to [code]data:[/code] URIs while loading. The renderer resolves no external paths, so without this an SVG that references a sibling image renders incomplete here while looking correct in a browser. Inlining also makes the exported markup self-contained. JPEG and WebP references are re-encoded as PNG, the one raster format the renderer is built with.

How the document is scaled into the content box when the node's size differs from [method get_intrinsic_size], mirroring CSS [code]object-fit[/code]. This is applied by writing [code]viewBox[/code] and [code]preserveAspectRatio[/code] onto the rendered root rather than by transforming on the Godot side, so a browser handed the same markup reaches the same result by specification rather than by a matching implementation. When the document declares no [code]viewBox[/code], one is synthesized from the intrinsic size.

Where the document sits inside the content box when [member fit] preserves its aspect ratio. Corresponds to the alignment half of [code]preserveAspectRatio[/code]. Has no effect when [member fit] is [constant FIT_NONE] or [constant FIT_FILL].

Whether child [WebSVGAnimation] elements play on the canvas. During playback the typed child DOM is serialized every frame with the current animated values (re-rasterizing only when the document changed), so raw markup extras such as [code]<defs>[/code] are not rendered while an animation is active. Serialized markup always includes the SMIL tags regardless of this setting.

constants.constant: The document came from [member svg_source] or [member svg_file_path].
Build the scriptable DOM for markup, and for a file only when it contains SMIL animation that needs it.
Always build the scriptable DOM, whatever the document's size or origin.
Never build the scriptable DOM. The fastest option for a large imported file, at the cost of not being able to address its shapes from code.

Honor the document's own [code]viewBox[/code] and [code]preserveAspectRatio[/code]. A document with a [code]viewBox[/code] scales to the content box the way a browser would; one without renders at 1:1 and is clipped.
Scale to fit entirely inside the content box, preserving the aspect ratio. CSS [code]object-fit: contain[/code], SVG [code]meet[/code].
Scale to cover the content box, preserving the aspect ratio and clipping the overflow. CSS [code]object-fit: cover[/code], SVG [code]slice[/code].
Stretch to fill the content box, ignoring the aspect ratio. CSS [code]object-fit: fill[/code], SVG [code]preserveAspectRatio="none"[/code].

Behaves as [constant FIT_NONE] when the content box is at least as large as the document, and as [constant FIT_CONTAIN] otherwise, so artwork is shrunk to fit but never enlarged. CSS [code]object-fit: scale-down[/code].

theme_items.theme_item: How the node size maps to the box. Numeric values are: [code]0[/code] = [code]Content Box[/code] / CSS [code]content-box[/code] (CSS default; the node size is the SVG content area and border + padding grow outward), [code]1[/code] = [code]Border Box[/code] / CSS [code]border-box[/code] (the node size is the border box and the content area shrinks). CSS [code]box-sizing[/code].
Inner spacing in pixels between the bottom border and the SVG content. CSS [code]padding-bottom[/code].
Inner spacing in pixels between the left border and the SVG content. CSS [code]padding-left[/code].
Inner spacing in pixels between the right border and the SVG content. CSS [code]padding-right[/code].
Inner spacing in pixels between the top border and the SVG content. CSS [code]padding-top[/code].
Fill color applied to child SVG shapes that do not set their own [code]fill[/code]. Matches the SVG default of opaque black.
Stroke color applied to child SVG shapes that do not set their own [code]stroke[/code]. Matches the SVG default of no stroke (transparent).
Stroke width in pixels applied to child SVG shapes that do not set their own [code]stroke-width[/code]. Matches the SVG default of [code]1[/code].

The [StyleBoxCSS] that paints this element's CSS box: background, border, border-radius, padding and box-shadow. The WebSVG [theme_item box_sizing] theme constant controls whether the node size is interpreted as the content box or border box. The default reproduces the browser user-agent stylesheet for [code]<svg>[/code] (transparent background, no border, no shadow and zero padding).
